skills.name: python-async-deadlock-debugger
skills.title: Python Async Deadlock Debugger
skills.description: Diagnose and fix hangs, deadlocks, livelocks and starvation in asyncio, threaded and multiprocessing Python: classify CPU spin vs blocked IO vs deadlock vs lost wakeup vs event loop blocked by sync code, collect evidence with faulthandler, py-spy dump, gdb py-bt, asyncio.all_tasks, python -m asyncio ps/pstree, debug mode and sys._current_frames, then fix lock-order cycles, non-reentrant asyncio.Lock re-acquisition, run_coroutine_threadsafe().result() on the loop thread, Queue.join without task_done, Condition lost wakeups, semaphore leaks, futures nobody resolves, nested event loops, thread pool exhaustion, multiprocessing Queue/fork deadlocks and shutdown hangs. Ships a static hang scanner and a watchdog that dumps every thread and asyncio task. Use when a Python program, agent loop, eval harness, embedding job, FastAPI service or GPU worker hangs, freezes, stops making progress, gets stuck at 99%, ignores Ctrl+C, never exits, or a test times out.

skills.name: python-asyncio-pattern-advisor
skills.title: Python Asyncio Pattern Advisor
skills.description: Recommend, implement and review Python asyncio patterns: async vs threads vs processes (IO vs CPU-bound), coroutines vs tasks vs futures, TaskGroup, gather and return_exceptions, wait and as_completed, Semaphore and Queue worker pools with backpressure, asyncio.timeout vs wait_for, cancellation, shield and cleanup, token-bucket RPM/TPM rate limits for LLM APIs, retries with backoff and jitter, async generators and SSE token streaming, to_thread/run_in_executor, background task references, eager tasks, asyncio.run/Runner, uvloop, Jupyter, FastAPI async vs def routes, httpx.AsyncClient lifespan, async DB/vector-store clients, debug mode and pytest-asyncio. Use when the user writes or reviews async def code, fans out LLM/embedding/scraping calls, hits 429s, sees 'coroutine was never awaited', 'Task exception was never retrieved', 'asyncio.run() cannot be called from a running event loop', 'This event loop is already running', hangs, slow callbacks or tasks that will not cancel, or asks gather vs TaskGroup.

skills.name: python-beginner-concept-tutor
skills.title: Python Beginner Concept Tutor
skills.description: Teach Python concepts to beginners heading into AI engineering (data scientists, analysts, students, career switchers): plain-language definitions, analogies, minimal examples, line-by-line walkthroughs, common mistakes, check-your-understanding questions and mini exercises; Socratic hints before solutions; explaining tracebacks; mutable vs immutable, references and aliasing, is vs ==, integer division, floating point, slicing and off-by-one, indentation errors; a staged learning path from variables to calling an LLM API, embeddings and a tiny RAG. Ships a script that lists the concepts a snippet uses in learning order and traces execution step by step like Python Tutor. Use when someone says they are new to Python, asks what a piece of code does line by line, asks to explain a concept or an error message simply, wants exercises or a study plan, or is learning Python to build LLM apps.

skills.name: python-comprehension-refactorer
skills.title: Python Comprehension Refactorer
skills.description: Refactor Python loops into list, dict and set comprehensions and generator expressions, and unroll comprehensions that are too clever: filtering, mapping, nested-loop flattening, conditional expressions, walrus in comprehensions, dict inversion, grouping with defaultdict/Counter, lazy generators for sum/any/all/max, streaming large files, itertools (chain, islice, groupby, batched, pairwise, accumulate, product), scoping rules, side-effect anti-patterns and performance (when map/filter or numpy/pandas vectorization win). AI-engineering focus: building prompt lists, batching texts for embeddings, filtering retrieved chunks by score, id->embedding dicts, flattening tool-call results, lazy dataset streaming and token counting. Use when the user asks to make a loop more Pythonic, convert a for loop to a comprehension, simplify or explain a nested comprehension, reduce memory with generators, batch or chunk an iterable, or review .py code for comprehension anti-patterns.

skills.name: python-context-manager-writer
skills.title: Python Context Manager Writer
skills.description: Write correct Python context managers and find resource-handling bugs — __enter__/__exit__ semantics and exception suppression, contextlib (contextmanager, asynccontextmanager, ExitStack, AsyncExitStack, closing, aclosing, suppress, redirect_stdout, nullcontext, chdir), async with, re-entrancy, leaked files/connections/clients/pools/locks, and AI-engineering recipes: torch.no_grad/inference_mode/autocast, eval()/train() switches, GPU cache cleanup, token and latency meters, tracing spans, temp env vars, rate-limit semaphores, httpx/aiohttp client lifecycle, FastAPI lifespan, DB/vector-store transactions, atomic checkpoint writes, seeds and agent sandboxes. Use when writing or reviewing a with statement or context manager, when files/sockets/clients/sessions/locks are opened without with, when an error is silently swallowed by __exit__ or a @contextmanager, on ResourceWarning, Too many open files, deadlocks, or generator didn't stop errors, or when wiring setup/teardown for models, clients and transactions.

skills.name: python-dataclass-converter
skills.title: Python Dataclass Converter
skills.description: Convert boilerplate Python classes, dicts, tuples and JSON payloads into dataclasses, or into pydantic v2 BaseModel, TypedDict, NamedTuple, attrs or msgspec when that fits better. Covers every @dataclass option (frozen, slots, kw_only, order, unsafe_hash, match_args, weakref_slot), field() (default_factory, init=False, repr, compare, hash, metadata), __post_init__, InitVar, KW_ONLY, inheritance and default ordering, replace(), asdict deep-copy pitfalls, hashing/equality, serialization and validation. AI focus: LLM request/response and chat Message types, RAG chunks with embeddings (numpy eq gotcha), eval records, configs, typed OpenAI/Anthropic JSON. Use when the user asks to convert a class or dict to a dataclass, remove __init__/__repr__/__eq__ boilerplate, model a JSON/API response with types, pick dataclass vs pydantic vs TypedDict, or fix dataclass errors (mutable default, non-default argument follows default argument, FrozenInstanceError, unhashable type).

skills.name: python-exception-handling-designer
skills.title: Python Exception Handling Designer
skills.description: Design and review Python exception handling: custom exception hierarchies with retryable flags, what to catch where, EAFP vs LBYL, chaining with raise ... from, else/finally, logger.exception, add_note, ExceptionGroup and except* with asyncio.TaskGroup, warnings, asserts vs validation, FastAPI error translation, retries with backoff and jitter, timeouts, cancellation, pytest.raises, plus LLM-app failures: 429 rate limits with retry-after, 5xx overloaded, context-length exceeded, content filters, broken streams, malformed JSON repair loops, tool-call errors fed back to the model, partial embedding batch failures, CUDA OOM batch halving, vector DB outages, circuit breakers and model fallbacks. Use when the user writes or reviews try/except code, designs an errors.py, asks how to retry or handle LLM/API errors, sees swallowed or lost tracebacks, maps exceptions to HTTP status codes, or tests exceptions in .py files.

skills.name: python-gil-bottleneck-analyzer
skills.title: Python GIL Bottleneck Analyzer
skills.description: Find out why Python code does not scale across cores and pick the right fix: what the GIL does and does not block (I/O, numpy, hashlib, zlib, re, json, Rust tokenizers, switch interval), classify workloads as pure-Python CPU, GIL-releasing native, I/O-bound, memory-bandwidth-bound or lock-contended, measure wall vs CPU time and speedup curves, profile with cProfile, py-spy (--gil, --idle, --native), Scalene, perf -X perf, viztracer, line_profiler, tracemalloc and sys.monitoring, free-threaded 3.13t/3.14t (PEP 703/779, PYTHON_GIL, sys._is_gil_enabled), subinterpreters and InterpreterPoolExecutor, processes, numpy/polars vectorisation, numba nogil, Cython, mypyc, pyo3, OMP_NUM_THREADS oversubscription. Use when threads give no speedup, CPU sits at 100% of one core, a FastAPI endpoint stalls under CPU work, tokenization, JSON parsing, regex cleaning, pandas apply, reranking or data loading is slow, or someone asks whether the GIL is the bottleneck.

skills.name: python-idiomatic-code-reviewer
skills.title: Python Idiomatic Code Reviewer
skills.description: Review Python code for non-idiomatic, unpythonic or risky patterns and rewrite it into clean modern Python: PEP 8 / PEP 20, EAFP vs LBYL, iteration idioms (enumerate, zip, comprehensions, any/all), unpacking, f-strings, pathlib, truthiness, `is None`, mutable defaults, walrus, match statements, collections / itertools / functools, logging instead of print, with-blocks and resource handling. Includes AI-engineering checks: hardcoded API keys, time.sleep or requests inside async def, missing HTTP timeouts, unbounded retry loops, model clients built at import time, prompt string concatenation, sequential awaits, eval() on LLM output. Ships a 46-rule AST reviewer with severities and suggested rewrites. Use when the user asks to review, clean up, modernise, make pythonic or idiomatic, refactor or code-review a .py file, LLM / RAG / agent / FastAPI / training code, a pull request diff, or asks 'is this good Python?' or 'how would a senior Python dev write this?'.

skills.name: python-multiprocessing-pool-designer
skills.title: Python Multiprocessing Pool Designer
skills.description: Design correct, fast process-based parallelism in Python: when processes beat threads/asyncio for CPU-bound code (and when free-threaded 3.13t/3.14t wins), multiprocessing.Pool (map, imap_unordered, starmap, apply_async callbacks), ProcessPoolExecutor (as_completed, max_tasks_per_child, mp_context, initializer), InterpreterPoolExecutor, fork vs spawn vs forkserver (3.14 Linux default), the __main__ guard, pickling rules, chunksize and IPC math, sizing workers to cores, cgroups and memory, per-worker model loading, copy-on-write and gc.freeze, shared_memory with numpy, Manager proxies, worker tracebacks, BrokenProcessPool, timeouts, Ctrl-C, worker logging, seeds, joblib/Ray/Dask/DataLoader. Ships a linter and a capacity planner. Use when parallelizing PDF/HTML parsing, chunking, tokenization, CPU embedding, image preprocessing, eval scoring or minhash dedup, or on PicklingError, BrokenProcessPool, 'bootstrapping phase', 'Cannot re-initialize CUDA in forked subprocess', or a pool slower than serial.

skills.name: python-threadpool-executor-builder
skills.title: Python ThreadPool Executor Builder
skills.description: Build correct, production-grade thread-based concurrency for I/O-bound Python: ThreadPoolExecutor submit/map/as_completed/wait (FIRST_COMPLETED, FIRST_EXCEPTION), Future callbacks, shutdown(cancel_futures), default max_workers (min(32, cpu+4), process_cpu_count in 3.13), initializer, BrokenThreadPool, Little's-law sizing, bounded submission and sliding windows, map buffersize (3.14), token-bucket RPM limiting, retries with backoff and jitter, cooperative cancellation, Ctrl-C, progress, thread-safe clients (requests.Session per thread, httpx, boto3, sqlite3), locks, queues, contextvars propagation, asyncio.to_thread and run_coroutine_threadsafe, free-threading, and testing. Ships a 19-rule linter and recipes. Use when fanning out LLM, embedding, scraping, S3 or vector-store calls from sync code, building an eval harness, or on lost exceptions, 429s, memory blowups from submit loops, hangs at exit, Ctrl-C ignored, 'cannot schedule new futures after shutdown' or 'Connection pool is full'.

skills.name: python-trio-anyio-migrator
skills.title: Python Trio / AnyIO Migrator
skills.description: Migrate asyncio code to AnyIO (runs on asyncio or trio) or to trio, and decide whether to migrate at all: structured concurrency (nurseries, task groups, cancel scopes, level-triggered cancellation, checkpoints), a complete asyncio -> anyio -> trio API map (run, sleep, gather/TaskGroup -> create_task_group/start_soon, tg.start and task_status, wait_for/timeout -> fail_after/move_on_after, shield, Event/Lock/Semaphore/CapacityLimiter, Queue -> memory object streams, to_thread, from_thread and blocking portals, run_process, signals), ExceptionGroup and except*, pytest anyio plugin, trio MockClock, httpx/Starlette/FastAPI vs asyncpg/aiohttp compatibility. skills.title: Python Type Hints Annotator

skills.name: rust-borrow-checker-error-explainer
skills.title: Rust Borrow Checker Error Explainer
skills.description: Explain and fix Rust borrow-checker, ownership, move and lifetime compiler errors: E0382 use of moved value, E0499 cannot borrow as mutable more than once, E0502 also borrowed as immutable, E0505, E0506, E0503, E0507 cannot move out of index/Rc/reference, E0515 return reference to local, E0597 does not live long enough, E0716 temporary value dropped while borrowed, E0373 closure may outlive (spawn needs move), E0521 borrowed data escapes, E0384, E0596, E0594, E0381, E0713, 'lifetime may not live long enough', RefCell 'already borrowed: BorrowMutError' panics. Ranks fixes from restructuring (split borrows, entry API, split_at_mut, get_disjoint_mut, mem::take, Option::take, indices, thread::scope) down to clone and Rc<RefCell>/Arc<Mutex>; never unsafe. Covers NLL limits (get-or-insert), iterator invalidation, closure captures, self-referential structs. Ships std-only Rust triage tools. Use when Rust fails to compile with a borrow/ownership error or the user is fighting the borrow checker.

skills.name: rust-cargo-workspace-designer

Use when the user creates or restructures a Rust monorepo, asks how to organise crates, sees 'profiles for the non root package will be ignored', 'cyclic package dependency', 'believes it's in a workspace when it's not', resolver warnings, duplicate dependency versions, slow builds or failed publishes.

skills.name: rust-error-handling-thiserror-anyhow-designer
skills.title: Rust Error Handling Designer (thiserror + anyhow)
